title: Pairing Four Points
problem: Four labeled points lie on a circle. Choose uniformly one of the three ways to pair them and draw the two straight chords joining each pair. What is the probability the chords cross inside the circle?

hints.text: List the three perfect matchings of four cyclically ordered points.
Two matchings use boundary sides; only the matching of opposite points creates two diagonals.

solution.setup: Label the cyclic points A,B,C,D. Their three pairings are AB|CD, AC|BD, and AD|BC.
solution.reasoning: In AB|CD and AD|BC, the chords are disjoint boundary sides. In AC|BD, both chords are diagonals and cross. Exactly one of three equally likely pairings crosses.
solution.sanityCheck: A convex quadrilateral has exactly one pair of crossing diagonals, matching the unique crossing pairing.

keyInsight: Symmetry reduces the geometry to three equally likely combinatorial matchings.
recognitionCues: A random geometric construction on symmetric labeled points may be counted through its discrete pairing types.
commonMistakes: Treating the six individual chords as independent choices.
followUps: For more points, what is the expected number of crossings in a random matching?

verification.notes: One of three perfect matchings crosses.
